items.title: Euro futures close below 1.10 at new year-to-date low.
items.excerpt: Euro futures extended their decline to close below the 1.10 level, marking a new year-to-date low and falling more than 2% since last week. The downward momentum initially began alongside a firmer U.S. dollar as market expectations around interest rate hikes shifted, before accelerating in recent sessions. As the euro moved lower, implied volatility tracked by the CME Group CVOL index continued to climb higher. Meanwhile, positioning data from last week revealed that speculators exited their net short positions rather than adding to them, marking the largest positioning reversal since the summer.

items.title: Tech stocks drag equity futures lower ahead of Fed remarks.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino of Path Trading Partners breaks down today's market action as U.S. equity futures trade lower, led by a 2.12% drop in E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures alongside declines in metals, crude oil and Bitcoin futures. Treasury yields edge down slightly from last week's highs. Traders are watching for remarks from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and New York Fed President John Williams in San Francisco regarding artificial intelligence, productivity and the labor market. Plus, a look ahead to this week's U.S.-China trade and technology talks in Shenzhen, corporate earnings and upcoming global economic releases including Reserve Bank of Australia minutes, U.K. employment, European economic sentiment, U.S. retail sales and industrial production.

items.title: Euro FX futures drop for 4th straight session on soft jobs data.
items.excerpt: Euro FX futures declined for a fourth consecutive session on Friday, extending a four-day drop to about 1.8% and tracking toward a fourth straight weekly loss of 1.07%. During the session, prices reached a high of 1.1086 before sliding to a low of 1.1038. On the economic front, third-quarter eurozone GDP rose 0.4% quarter over quarter, matching expectations, while quarterly employment remained flat against estimates for a 0.2% increase and annual employment growth slowed from 0.5% to 0.4%. Meanwhile, the European Central Bank reiterated a meeting-by-meeting policy approach while noting higher energy costs could elevate inflation and weigh on growth. Markets currently anticipate December rate hikes from both the ECB and the Federal Reserve, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.

items.title: From GTA VI to Formula 1: why the future of investing could be entertainment
items.excerpt: Key takeaways Gaming, sports and live entertainment can turn loyal audiences into revenue streams that last for years. Unique franchises, global fan bases and experiences that are difficult to replicate can create lasting competitive advantages. Popularity alone is not an investment case. Profitability, growth expectations and the price investors pay still matter. The business of having fun On 19 November 2026, Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI), one of the most anticipated video games in history, is scheduled to launch . Its publisher, Take-Two Interactive, reported exceptionally strong pre-orders this week and raised its annual revenue forecast. But for investors, the bigger story is not how many copies GTA VI sells next week. It is how much money the game could generate over the next decade.

items.title: Swiss Franc futures tumble to worst day since March.
items.excerpt: Swiss Franc futures declined sharply against the U.S. dollar, dropping 1.06% to an intraday low of 1.2040 to register their largest single-day percentage decline since March 2. Greenback strength expanded after core CPI increased 0.3% month over month, hitting the threshold Fed Governor Christopher Waller indicated would open discussion for a 50 bps move. The CME FedWatch Tool now fully prices a December policy increase, reflecting an 86.9% probability of a 25 bps hike and a 13.1% chance of a half-point adjustment. Meanwhile, the Swiss National Bank maintains its policy rate at zero with inflation remaining contained, setting up potential further policy divergence between the two central banks.
